# NASA’s SpaceX Crew-11 Mission

## Viewing Posts from August 2025

![Expedition 73 welcomes NASA's SpaceX Crew-11 mission aboard the International Space Station. In the front from left are, Crew-11 members Oleg Platonov, Mike Fincke, Zena Cardman, and Kimiya Yui. In the back are, Expedition 73 members Takuya Onishi, Kirill Peskov, Alexey Zubritsky, Sergey Ryzhikov, Jonny Kim, Nichole Ayers, and Anne McClain.](https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/blog-exp73-11-member-crew-080425.jpg?w=900)

NASA astronauts Zena Cardman and Mike Fincke, JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) astronaut Kimiya Yui, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Oleg Platonov arrived at the International Space Station as the SpaceX Dragon spacecraft docked to the orbiting complex at 2:27 a.m.

excerpts.text: **SpaceX Crew-11** was the eleventh operational NASA [Commercial Crew Program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commercial_Crew_Program "Commercial Crew Program") flight and the 19th crewed orbital flight of a [Crew Dragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crew_Dragon "Crew Dragon") spacecraft. The mission transported four crew members, [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") astronauts [Zena Cardman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zena_Cardman "Zena Cardman") and [Michael Fincke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Fincke "Michael Fincke"), [JAXA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JAXA "JAXA") astronaut [Kimiya Yui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimiya_Yui "Kimiya Yui"), and [Roscosmos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roscosmos "Roscosmos") cosmonaut [Oleg Platonov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oleg_Platonov_(cosmonaut) "Oleg Platonov (cosmonaut)"), to the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") (ISS). The mission launched on August 1, 2025 and docked with the ISS the next day. On January 8, 2026, NASA announced that the mission would end about a month earlier than planned due to a medical situation involving Fincke.

assessment.rationale: The spans confirm a Crew-11 launch attempt was postponed to August 1, 2025, from July 31, 2025, due to weather, and was to launch from Kennedy Space Center in Florida. However, the number of astronauts is not mentioned.

excerpts.text:
![A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket with the company’s Dragon spacecraft on top is seen on the launch pad at Launch Complex 39A at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Thursday, July 31, 2025, ahead of the agency’s SpaceX Crew-11 launch.](https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/screenshot-31-7-2025-12134.jpeg?w=1275)

An unfavorable weather forecast for the launch site at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida for Thursday afternoon has resulted in NASA and SpaceX postponing the launch of the Crew-11 crew. Teams are now targeting 11:43 a.m. EDT Friday, Aug. 1.

NASA’s live launch coverage for an Aug. 1 attempt begins at 7:35 a.m. on [NASA+](https://plus.nasa.gov/scheduled-video/nasas-spacex-crew-11-launch/).
